coordinates.locator: Wikipedia, "Waste Isolation Pilot Plant", infobox coordinates
coordinates.note: No official DOE/WIPP page or technical/geodetic paper consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states coordinates; this is the site's general campus/surface location per Wikipedia only, shown as approximate. EXO-200's own underground placement (~655 m below this surface point) is recorded on the detector's placement note rather than as a separate detector-grade coordinate, since no primary or official source gives an underground coordinate distinct from this campus point.

depth.note: Converted from the quoted feet figure (2,150 ft x 0.3048 = 655.3 m).
depth.quote: Transuranic waste is disposed of 2,150 feet underground in rooms mined from the salt bed.

depth_mwe.locator: The EXO-200 detector, part I: Detector design and construction (arXiv:1202.2192), site description
depth_mwe.note: The figure is from the EXO-200 detector design paper (arXiv:1202.2192), read directly on 2026-09-17. A later EXO-200 paper (Searches for Double Beta Decay of 134Xe with EXO-200) instead reports ~1624 (+22/−21) m.w.e. for the underground clean room; this later re-estimate was not checked against the paper itself. The detector design paper's 1585 m.w.e. is recorded as the directly sourced value; the difference between the two figures is unresolved. The WIPP muon-flux paper (Esch et al. 2005), converting its own measured flux, gives 1585 (+11/-6) m.w.e. at 655 m depth with a salt density of 2.3 ± 0.2 g/cm^3, in agreement with the EXO-200 design paper's figure.
depth_mwe.quote: EXO-200 is located at a depth of 1585 m water equivalent ... in the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP) near Carlsbad, New Mexico

muon_flux.locator: Esch et al. 2005, Sec. 3.2, Eq. (9); Mei & Hime 2006, Table I (WIPP row)
muon_flux.note: The quote is the WIPP row of Mei & Hime Table I (total flux in cm^-2 s^-1, then equivalent depth in km.w.e.), which cites Esch et al.; Esch et al. state their total flux as (4.77 +0.08/-0.10) × 10^-7 Hz/cm^2 through two stacked scintillator panels (area 2.33 m^2, run time 532800 s), corrected for geometric efficiency. Their vertical intensity, (3.10 +0.05/-0.07) × 10^-7 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1, is not a flux and is not recorded. Measured in the Q area at 655 m depth. Woodley et al. 2024 Table III repeats (4.77 ± 0.09) × 10^-7.

name: WIPP surface campus, Carlsbad, New Mexico
notes: This is a campus-level approximate marker (Wikipedia-sourced), not a detector-grade coordinate; EXO-200's underground hall and clean-room position is unsourced and is not given a detector-grade marker.

The water-equivalent depth is the 1585 m.w.e. stated in the EXO-200 detector design paper (arXiv:1202.2192). A later EXO-200 paper reports ~1624 (+22/−21) m.w.e. instead (a subsequent re-estimate, not checked against the paper itself); see the note on the depth value.

summary.plain: A patch of New Mexico desert above a deep salt mine. The mine below stores nuclear waste, and from 2011 to 2018 also housed the EXO-200 neutrino experiment.
summary.technical: Surface campus of WIPP near Carlsbad, New Mexico; underground rooms ~655 m below in a Permian salt bed hosted the EXO-200 136Xe TPC 2011-2018.
